MCP connection
links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a

. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems.
Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically.

Frequently asked questions
What is the Discord API rate limit for bots?
Two layers. Globally, a bot may make 50 requests per second across all endpoints. Separately, each route has its own bucket whose size Discord does not publish; you read it from the X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers on every response, and X-RateLimit-Bucket tells you which routes share a bucket. - MCP resources for accessing Klaviyo data
- Easy integration with LLMs via the Model

## Setup

1. Clone this repository
2. Install dependencies:
   ```
   npm install
   ```
3. Create a `.env` file based on `.env.example` and add your Klaviyo API key:
   ```
   KLAVIYO_API_KEY=your_private_api_key_here
   ```
4. Start the server:
   ```
   npm run dev
   ```

## Testing with MCP Inspector

You can test the server using the MCP Inspector:

```
npm run inspect
```

This will open a web interface where you can test all the available tools and resources.

GraphQL models a business domain as a graph using a schema. In the schema, there are logical definitions for different types of nodes and their connections (edges). These nodes are the datasets you use for your analytics. You write queries in GraphQL much like in SQL: you specify the dataset (table), the metrics to retrieve (such as requests and bytes), and filter or group by dimensions (for example, a time period).
GraphQL differs from a traditional API: it has one single endpoint:
https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql

Get Started
Sentry bills differently than most observability platforms: instead of metering data volume, it meters events, errors, spans, replays, logs, and attachments each with its own quota and its own overage rate. Overages on the Team plan run from $0.0003625 per error in the 50k–100k tier down to $0.0001500 per error at 20M+ events, while Business tier overage rates run higher, from $0.0011125 per error down to $0.0003000 at the top tier. An internal connection is scoped to a single Notion workspace. Only members of that workspace can use it. Internal connections are ideal for team-owned automations and workflows — things like syncing data from external tools, sending notifications when pages change, or powering internal dashboards.

evidence.excerpt:
Atlassian platform GraphQL API makes this data accessible using one common mechanism using the Atlassian GraphQL Gateway.
About GraphQL
GraphQL
is a query language for APIs. This style of API allows access to
linked data, which you can think of as a
graph of entities
.
For example, you can request the work activity of a team of people and get the details for those
people in the same request. With other types of APIs, such as REST APIs, this would require many
requests, making GraphQL more efficient and flexible to use.
Because you must specify the data attributes you want back (called
fields
), the payloads can be
smaller and hence faster over the network.  In other words, you only get the data that you specified
and no more.
